questions.q: Who is the prophet lamenting?
questions.a: The people of Israel are the ones the prophet is mourning over.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to a town that sends out a thousand soldiers to fight?
questions.a: A town that sends out a thousand soldiers to fight will have only a hundred who survive.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people of Israel to do?
questions.a: Yahweh tells the people of Israel to sincerely worship him again him so they can live.

questions.q: What three places does Yahweh tell the people not to go to worship?
questions.a: Yahweh tells them not to go to Bethel, Gilgal, or Beersheba.

questions.q: What will happen to the house of Joseph if they do not seek Yahweh?
questions.a: Yahweh will destroy them completely, and no one will be able to stop it.

questions.q: How do the people treat justice and righteousness, according to Yahweh?
questions.a: They make unjust decisions, and they completely reject right living.

questions.q: What is the name of the one who made the stars, turns darkness into morning, and makes the waters of the sea into rain that falls on the whole earth?
questions.a: His name is Yahweh.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do to those who are strong?
questions.a: Yahweh brings sudden destruction on the strong.

questions.q: Who do the strong hate and abhor?
questions.a: The strong hate those who correct them, and abhor anyone who speaks the truth.

questions.q: What will happen to those who oppress the poor?
questions.a: Those who oppress the poor will not benefit from the things they work for.

questions.q: What do the people do to the needy at the gate?
questions.a: They treat the needy unjustly and send them away when they bring their legal matters to the leaders to decide.

questions.q: What does a prudent person do at such an evil time?
questions.a: A prudent person stays silent at such an evil time.

questions.q: What should the people do so that Yahweh will be with them?
questions.a: The people should try to do good and not evil, so that Yahweh will be with them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people to do, so that he might be gracious to the remnant of Joseph?
questions.a: Yahweh tells them to hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the gate.

questions.q: What will be heard in all the public places when Yahweh comes to punish them?
questions.a: Wailing and cries of mourning will be heard in all the public places when Yahweh passes through the people’s midst to punish them.

questions.q: What will happen to those who are desiring the day of Yahweh to come?
questions.a: Terrible things will happen to them; the day of Yahweh will be darkness, not light.

questions.q: What happens to a man in this illustration who flees from a lion?
questions.a: He flees the lion only to have a bear meet him, and he goes into his house to be safe only to have a snake bite him.

questions.q: What will the day of Yahweh be?
questions.a: The day of Yahweh will be a time of punishment for his people that will make them deeply sad.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the people’s feasts and assemblies?
questions.a: Yahweh says he hates their religious celebrations and their assemblies.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do if the people offer him burnt offerings and grain offerings?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will not accept them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the people’s songs and music?
questions.a: Yahweh says their songs are just noise to him, and he will not listen to their music.

questions.q: What does Yahweh want to see people continually doing?
questions.a: Yahweh wants to see people treating people fairly and doing what is right.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the people did not bring him during the forty years in the wilderness?
questions.a: Yahweh says they did not bring him sacrifices and grain offerings.

questions.q: What had the people made for themselves?
questions.a: The people had made for themselves idols that were images of the false gods they were worshiping.

questions.q: Where will Yahweh send the people?
questions.a: Yahweh will exile the people beyond Damascus.

commentary.text: Israel is called to seek the Lord.

Verses 1–6 The convincing, awakening word must be heard and heeded, as well as words of comfort and peace; for whether we hear or forbear, the word of God shall take effect. The Lord still proclaims mercy to men, but they often expect deliverance from such self-invented forms as make their condemnation sure. While they refuse to come to Christ and to seek mercy in and by him, that they may live, the fire of Divine wrath breaks forth upon them. Men may make an idol of the world, but will find it cannot protect.

The same almighty power can, for repenting sinners, easily turn affliction and sorrow into prosperity and joy, and as easily turn the prosperity of daring sinners into utter darkness. Evil times will not bear plain dealing; that is, evil men will not. And these men were evil men indeed, when wise and good men thought it in vain even to speak to them. Those who will seek and love that which is good, may help to save the land from ruin. It behoves us to plead God's spiritual promises, to beseech him to create in us a clean heart, and to renew a right spirit within us. The Lord is ever ready to be gracious to the souls that seek him; and then piety and every duty will be attended to. But as for sinful Israel, God's judgments had often passed by them, now they shall pass through them.

Woe unto those that desire the day of the Lord's judgments, that wish for times of war and confusion; as some who long for changes, hoping to rise upon the ruins of their country! but this should be so great a desolation, that nobody could gain by it. The day of the Lord will be a dark, dismal, gloomy day to all impenitent sinners. When God makes a day dark, all the world cannot make it light. Those who are not reformed by the judgments of God, will be pursued by them; if they escape one, another stands ready to seize them. A pretence of piety is double iniquity, and so it will be found. The people of Israel copied the crimes of their forefathers. The law of worshipping the Lord our God, is, Him only we must serve. Professors thrive so little, because they have little or no communion with God in their duties. They were led captive by Satan into idolatry, therefore God caused them to go into captivity among idolaters.
